record.countingMethod: Conservative review-unit count: 83 glossary definitions (including aliases), 16 complete question/answer/distractor/worked-example units, 5 formula blocks, 16 analogy mapping/limitation paragraphs, and 8 runnable example/output units = 128. Every lesson’s remaining technical prose was also checked; it is not assigned an invented atomic-fact count or counted twice here.
corrections: Fixed-width integer glossary definition incorrectly counted the sign bit as a value bit. It now distinguishes total bit width, unsigned value bits, signed sign bit, no padding and the optional C11 two’s-complement exact-width types (N1570 7.20.1.1).

The inverted-mask example could be read as having identical promoted operand types on every C implementation. It now states the checked host’s 32-bit unsigned model and requires checking target promotions; UINT32_C follows the promoted uint_least32_t type (N1570 6.3.1.1, 7.20.4.1).

The PWM lesson could imply that every onboard indicator has a direct hardware PWM route. It now requires confirming a PWM-capable route and explains that indicators driven through another device may need a different interface; official Pico/Pico W blink implementation linked.

The PWM lesson categorically called a true DAC a different peripheral. It now describes a dedicated DAC as another method with settling/load constraints, avoiding a false boundary with switching DAC architectures. The DAC glossary source now points to Analog Devices MT-014, which actually supports its definition.
Bare glossary aliases bounds and resolution captured unrelated timing meanings. Removed them while retaining the specific array-bounds and ADC-resolution aliases.

The floor-quantiser definition used next lower boundary, ambiguous for an input exactly on a boundary. It now says lower boundary is at or below the input and explicitly limits this to the illustrative model.
gaps: This beginner module teaches safe reasoning and hosted models; it does not give a universal board wiring or raw-register recipe. Pin assignments, voltage limits, peripheral routes, register side effects and startup must be checked for the actual target.

No physical board, switch, ADC source or load was tested. The C, debounce, ADC-bin and PWM results are software/model checks; actual electrical behavior, bounce duration, converter transitions and PWM timing remain target-dependent, as stated in the lessons.
Real ADC acquisition design, calibration, analogue filtering, PWM load drivers and detailed C concurrency/dynamic allocation are deliberately outside these eight short introductory units.

analogyReview.scope: Independent review of all eight new active lesson analogy decisions, their mappings, limitations, surrounding required explanations and all questions with callouts closed.

esc-c-values-types.rationale: Added jar comparison helps separate a representable range from the value’s physical meaning. The explicit limit correctly says C names do not enforce units and conversion rules still apply (N1570 6.2.5, 6.3.1.3). Types, ranges and the narrowing result remain visible.

esc-pointers-registers.rationale: Added room/noticeboard comparison separates a pointer from a copied snapshot. The limit preserves C pointer validity and hardware read side effects; it does not suggest that any numeric address is safe. N1570 6.5.3.2 and the device register documentation support the mapping. Volatile limitations remain outside the callout.

esc-bits-masks.rationale: Added labelled-switch comparison correctly maps set/clear/toggle operations for ordinary integer values. Its limit explicitly excludes special register semantics and concurrent changes, as required by RP2040 register documentation. The mask arithmetic and visible RMW warning remain self-contained.

esc-gpio-input-output.rationale: Added door-sign comparison explains active polarity as an agreed interpretation of an electrical level. Its limit correctly retains voltage compatibility and direction as separate requirements (RP2040 electrical/GPIO documentation). All configuration and safety guidance remains visible.

esc-buttons-debounce.rationale: Added repeated-answer comparison maps candidate, consecutive count and accepted state to the actual algorithm. Its limit avoids claiming that samples prove continuous stability; Microchip AN2805 supports the need for an appropriate debounce interval. The complete trace and sample timing caveat remain visible.

esc-memory-lifetimes.rationale: Added borrowed-workbench comparison explains that holding a pointer does not extend object lifetime. Its limit accurately states that C does not enforce the booking and access after lifetime can be undefined (N1570 6.2.4). Visible text separately covers ownership, real capacity and the expired pointer.

esc-adc-samples.rationale: Added ruler comparison separates resolution from accuracy, consistent with RP2040 ADC specifications including ENOB and errors. Its limit preserves noise, acquisition timing and input-circuit constraints. The ideal floor-bin model and separate endpoint scaling caveat remain visible.

esc-pwm-output.rationale: Added tap comparison explains period and high-time fraction without claiming an intermediate digital voltage. Its limit explicitly rejects unlimited pin power and automatic harmless averaging. RP2040 PWM and electrical specifications support these boundaries; timer mode/count assumptions and safety remain visible.
